findings.source_quote: τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι χάριν οἶδα εἰληφώς, οὐ δεδωκώς
findings.english_quote: Hence I know that, in undertaking to oversee you, I have received a favor, not given one.
findings.issue: The draft makes Peter undertake the oversight of Clement. The stronger contextual analysis takes Clement as the subject of the infinitival undertaking: Clement undertakes to administer, and Peter regards that undertaking as a favor received. The nominative participles εἰληφώς and δεδωκώς establish Peter as the recipient rather than giver of the favor; they do not establish him as the subject of the embedded infinitives. The draft therefore assigns an administrative relationship that the supplied wording does not securely establish.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed replacement, not yet accepted: “Hence I know that, in your undertaking to administer, I have received a favor, not given one.” Review this proposal afresh after separately documenting the grammatical relationships among the articular infinitival expression, σέ, χάριν, and οἶδα.

findings.english_quote: A further, less explicit analysis makes Clement the subject of ἀναδέξασθαι as well, so that Clement undertakes the administration, but the change of subject is not overtly marked.
findings.issue: The source_issues note overlooks σέ as an overt possible accusative subject of the entire infinitival expression and consequently misranks the alternatives. The first-person subject of οἶδα must be distinguished from the subject of the embedded infinitives. The assignment of administration remains an unresolved source-meaning issue requiring separate grammatical evidence. The image-checked print establishes the supplied wording, not the interpretation; no corruption has been demonstrated.
findings.suggested_revision: Provide a separate grammatical assessment, supported by cited comparable Greek constructions, of σέ as subject of the entire infinitival expression versus object of οἰκονομεῖν. Rewrite the disclosure to reflect that evidence and preserve any remaining alternatives. Do not propose a Greek correction merely to regularize the construction. Keep the passage blocked pending that assessment and fresh review of the English.

findings.source_quote: ἵνα ἕκαστος, ἐπιδικαζόμενος τοῦ πάντας φίλους ἔχειν, αὐτὸν διαλλάττων σώζηται
findings.english_quote: so that each person, pressing his claim to have everyone as friends, may be saved by reconciling him
findings.issue: The English preserves the active construction with αὐτόν as its object, but the identity of ἕκαστος, the referent of αὐτόν, and the relationship effected by διαλλάττων remain unresolved. The existing note discloses the uncertainty and marks it as publication-blocking. Adequate disclosure does not supply the separate evidence needed to resolve that hold. This is a source-meaning problem, not demonstrated corruption of the verified print.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the provisional wording and disclosure. Obtain a separate contextual and lexical assessment of ἐπιδικάζομαι with the genitive infinitival expression and of active διαλλάττω with a personal object and an unstated second party, supported by cited Greek usage. Do not insert a named referent or change the construction to self-reconciliation without that evidence. Any resulting replacement requires fresh review.

findings.issue: The possessive αὐτοῦ most naturally refers to the presiding leader, but its relationship to the unresolved preceding αὐτόν remains uncertain. The draft preserves the pronoun and discloses the alternative; it does not establish whose discourse is heeded. This separately disclosed blocking issue cannot be cleared merely by retaining neutral English.
findings.suggested_revision: Provide a separate antecedent analysis using the supplied paragraph, including the recurring references to the leader and the preceding reconciliation clause. Preserve the alternative if the evidence remains inconclusive. No correction to the Greek is presently justified, and the passage remains blocked.

findings.source_quote: Ἀξιῶ σε ἐπὶ πάντων μου τῶν συνπαρόντων ἀδελφῶν, ὅπως ὁπόταν τοῦ ἐνταῦθα (ὡς ἐμοὶ ὀφείλεται) ἀπαλλάξω βίου, σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον μέχρι καὶ τῶν ἐκ παίδων σου λογισμῶν καὶ ὡς ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς μέχρι τοῦ νῦν συνώδευσάς μοι, ἐπακούων τῶν κατὰ πόλιν ὑπ᾽ ἐμοῦ κηρυχθέντων λόγων τε καὶ πράξεων, ἔπειτα πρὸς τῷ τέλει καὶ τὴν τοῦ θανάτου μου πρόφασιν ὡς προεῖπον δηλῶσαι μὴ ὀκνήσῃς
findings.english_quote: Before all my brothers who are present with me, I ask you that, whenever I depart from this life here—as is owed to me—you not hesitate to send James, the Lord’s brother, a concise written account extending even to your thoughts from childhood and telling how, from the beginning until now, you have traveled with me, listening to the words and deeds proclaimed by me from city to city, and then, toward the end, also to make known the cause of my death, as I said beforehand.
findings.issue: The rendering defensibly takes the second σέ as a resumed subject of διαπέμψαι and ἀναγραψάμενον, understands the written account as the thing sent, and gives μὴ ὀκνήσῃς scope over both infinitival instructions. Nevertheless, those syntactic relationships remain unsettled, as the draft's blocking source_issues note acknowledges. Disclosure alone does not establish this construction or eliminate the alternatives. The unusual syntax does not itself demonstrate corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Obtain a separate grammatical assessment, supported by cited comparable constructions, of the resumed accusative after ὅπως and the temporal clause, the dependency of διαπέμψαι, and the scope of the final μὴ ὀκνήσῃς. Retain the provisional interpretation and alternatives until that evidence is assessed. Do not import wording from another edition or normalize the Greek to produce the preferred syntax. Review any revised English afresh.

findings.source_quote: οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς τὴν τοῦ διδάσκοντος ἐπιστεύθη καθέδραν
findings.english_quote: after me it was not to an unlearned man—one ignorant of life-giving words and not knowing the church’s rule—that the teacher’s chair was entrusted.
findings.issue: The main text gives the first οὐκ broad scope over the entrusting to the described recipient while preserving the explicit negation in οὐκ εἰδώς. This is coherent, but the competing local scope of the first negation remains unresolved. The draft discloses that blocking uncertainty. The printed period after κανόνα is a separate editorial feature, not evidence establishing either scope and not by itself evidence of corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Provide a separate syntactic assessment of the first negation's scope across the coordinated descriptions and delayed ἐπιστεύθη, supported by comparable Greek usage. Preserve both negations and the distinction between interpretive uncertainty and printed punctuation. Do not silently distribute the first negation across the participles, delete either negation, or treat the punctuation as a transcription error. Keep the passage blocked until the assessment and any resulting English undergo fresh review.

findings.source_quote: Κλήμεντος τῶν Πέτρου ἐπιδημίων κηρυγμάτων ἐπιτομή
findings.issue: The compound preserves ἐπιδημίων as qualifying the preachings, and the preceding city-by-city description supports an association with Peter's visits or stays. Nevertheless, the adjective's precise force remains unresolved between visit-associated and local/public senses. The existing disclosure identifies this as publication-blocking. The provisional compound does not itself resolve the lexical uncertainty, and no defect in the verified Greek has been established.
findings.suggested_revision: Provide separate, cited lexical evidence for ἐπιδήμιος in comparable literary contexts, explicitly distinguishing evidence for the adjective from evidence merely for cognate nouns or verbs. Assess that evidence against the supplied title and preceding description. Retain the provisional title and alternatives pending assessment; any replacement requires fresh review. Keep the discussion of ἐπιγράψαντα separate as a syntactic feature: ἐπιγράψας remains a proposed normalization, not an established correction.
